examples.en: A famous director directs this drama.
He directed the play himself.
I want to create a warm atmosphere.
The film I directed won an award.

examples.ko: 조명으로 밤 분위기를 연출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can create a night mood with lighting.

examples.ko: 연출하는 사람은 배우들과 이야기를 많이 해요.
examples.en: The person who directs talks a lot with the actors.

explain: 영화나 연극에서 '연출'은 감독이 하는 일이에요. 그래서 '연출자'라는 말도 있어요. 분위기나 장면을 일부러 만든다는 뜻으로 일상에서도 써요.

phrases.en: The director explains the scene to the actors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 연극을 연출하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who directs a film or play.

phrases.example: 그 감독이 새 영화 연출을 맡았어요.
phrases.en: That director took charge of the new movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연출하는 일을 책임진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being responsible for directing.

phrases.en: I create a warm mood with candles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기나 장면을 일부러 만든다는 뜻으로 일상에서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means deliberately creating a mood or scene; used in daily life too.

explain_en: In films and plays, '연출' is the director's job, which is why '연출자' exists. In everyday talk it also means deliberately setting up a mood or scene.

examples.en: That singer composes songs herself.
I have composed on the piano since I was little.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 생일을 위해 노래를 작곡해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend composed a song for my birthday.
Composing is hard but fun.
Who composed this song?

examples.ko: 올해 안에 앨범 전체를 작곡할 거예요.
examples.en: I will compose the whole album within this year.

explain: 곡을 만드는 건 '작곡', 가사를 쓰는 건 '작사'예요. 둘 다 하면 '작사 작곡'이라고 붙여 말해요. 곡을 만드는 사람은 '작곡가'예요.

phrases.example: 저는 언젠가 제 노래를 작곡하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: Someday I want to compose my own song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 일이나 꿈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what you want to do or dream of.

phrases.en: I am composing a new song right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something happening right now.

phrases.en: He wrote both the lyrics and the music of this song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가사와 곡을 모두 만들었을 때 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when someone made both the lyrics and the music.

explain_en: Making the music is '작곡' and writing the lyrics is '작사'. Someone who does both is described as '작사 작곡'. The person who writes music is a '작곡가' (composer).

examples.en: The officiant's speech was so long that the guests got bored.
I cried at my teacher's wedding speech.

examples.ko: 결혼식 때 들은 주례사를 아직도 기억해요.
examples.en: I still remember the speech I heard at the wedding.

examples.ko: 주례사는 보통 짧고 따뜻한 말이 좋아요.
examples.en: A wedding officiant's speech is best when it is short and warm.
In the speech, they said 'respect each other.'
These days many weddings don't have an officiant's speech.

explain: 결혼식에서 주례를 맡은 사람이 신랑 신부에게 해 주는 말이에요. 덕담이 중심이라 '덕담'과 비슷하게 따뜻한 조언이 많아요. 요즘은 주례 없이 하는 결혼식도 있어요.

phrases.en: The teacher gave remarks to the bride and groom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주례를 맡은 사람이 말하는 것을 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the officiant giving the speech.

phrases.en: The guests listened quietly to the remarks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the listener's point of view.

phrases.en: I'm officiating at my friend's wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼식을 진행하는 일을 맡는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means taking the role of wedding officiant.

explain_en: It is what the person officiating a wedding says to the bride and groom. It is mostly good wishes and warm advice, similar to '덕담'. Nowadays some weddings are held without an officiant.

examples.ko: 이 재즈 트리오는 연주가 정말 편안해요.
examples.en: This jazz trio's playing is really relaxing.

examples.ko: 친구 둘이랑 트리오를 만들어서 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: I formed a trio with two friends and we sang.

examples.ko: 피아노 트리오 공연을 보러 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to go see a piano trio concert.

examples.ko: 저희 세 사람은 학교에서 유명한 트리오예요.
examples.en: The three of us are a famous trio at school.

examples.ko: 그 트리오의 새 앨범이 다음 주에 나와요.
examples.en: That trio's new album comes out next week.

examples.ko: 바이올린, 첼로, 피아노로 이루어진 트리오가 연주했어요.
examples.en: A trio made up of violin, cello and piano performed.

explain: 음악에서 세 명이 함께하는 연주나 노래 팀에 주로 써요. 두 명이면 '듀오', 네 명이면 '콰르텟(사중주)'이라고 해요. 친한 세 사람을 장난스럽게 '트리오'라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.example: 저희는 세 명이 트리오로 활동하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The three of us perform as a trio.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세 명이 한 팀으로 음악 활동을 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means three people performing music together as one team.

phrases.en: I formed a trio with my college friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀을 새로 만든다는 말이에요. '그룹을 결성하다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means newly forming a team, like 'form a group'.

phrases.en: I went to a piano trio concert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피아노를 중심으로 세 악기가 함께 연주하는 음악 팀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A music group of three instruments centered on the piano.

explain_en: Trio — loanword for a group of three, mainly music (우리는 피아노, 바이올린, 첼로로 이루어진 트리오 공연을 봤어요.) It is mainly used for a group of three who play or sing together. Two people are a '듀오' and four are a '콰르텟' (quartet). People also playfully call three close friends a '트리오'.

t90.ax: I want to go see a piano trio concert.

examples.ko: 체조 선수가 평균대 위에서 균형을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The gymnast kept her balance on the balance beam.
A balance beam is only 10 centimeters wide.
My daughter fell while practicing on the balance beam.
The backward turn on the balance beam is hard.
She advanced to the balance beam final at this competition.

examples.ko: 평균대 위에서는 시선을 앞에 두는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: On the balance beam, it's important to keep your eyes ahead.

explain: 여자 체조 종목에 쓰는 좁고 긴 기구와 그 종목 이름이에요. 이름에 '평균'이 들어가지만 숫자의 평균이 아니라 균형(평균)을 잡는다는 뜻의 한자어예요. 그래서 수학 시간의 '평균'과는 관계가 없어요.

phrases.en: I watched a balance beam event on TV yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기구가 아니라 체조 종목 이름으로 쓸 때 '경기'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 경기 makes it refer to the gymnastics event, not just the apparatus.

phrases.en: The athlete fell off the balance beam and lost points.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기 중 실수를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for describing a mistake during a routine.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall off the balance beam

phrases.en: The child walked carefully along the balance beam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기구 자체를 말할 때 '위'와 함께 써서 균형 잡는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 위 (on top of) to describe the act of balancing on the apparatus itself.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk on the balance beam

explain_en: It is the narrow, long apparatus used in women's gymnastics, and also the event's name. '평균' here refers to balance, not the mathematical average, so it has nothing to do with the '평균' in math class.

en: to wriggle; to wiggle; to writhe

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에 땅에서 지렁이가 꿈틀대요.
examples.en: After the rain, earthworms wriggle on the ground.
Every time the baby moves in my belly, it feels amazing.

examples.ko: 마음속에서 화가 꿈틀대는 걸 겨우 참았어요.
examples.en: I barely held back the anger stirring inside me.
A snake slithered past through the grass.

examples.ko: 어항 속 물고기들이 바닥에서 꿈틀대고 있어요.
examples.en: The fish in the tank are wriggling along the bottom.

examples.ko: 새로운 일을 해 보고 싶은 마음이 자꾸 꿈틀대요.
examples.en: The desire to try something new keeps stirring in me.

explain: '꿈틀'이 한 번이면 '꿈틀대다'는 계속 반복해서 움직이는 느낌이에요. 욕망이나 감정이 마음속에서 움직일 때도 '욕심이 꿈틀대다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: A bug is wriggling on my palm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿈틀대다'와 뜻이 거의 같고 둘 다 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '꿈틀대다', and both are used often.

phrases.en: Seeing a nice item, my greed stirs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음속에서 욕심이나 감정이 움직이기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when desire or emotion starts to stir inside you.

phrases.en: Something is wriggling inside the box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 움직이는 중이라는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is moving continuously right now.

explain_en: Heavier, bigger wriggle of worms or caterpillars, repeated. If '꿈틀' is a single movement, '꿈틀대다' means moving repeatedly. It is also used for feelings, as in '욕심이 꿈틀대다' (greed stirs).

t90.ax: A snake slithered past through the grass.

examples.ko: 우리 집 누렁이는 산책을 정말 좋아해요.
examples.en: Our dog Nureongi loves walks so much.
Grandfather is feeding the yellow dog.

examples.ko: 시골 마당에서 누렁이가 꼬리를 흔들며 달려왔어요.
examples.en: In the countryside yard, the yellow dog came running, wagging its tail.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 키우던 누렁이 생각이 나요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of the yellow dog I had as a child.

examples.ko: 누렁이를 데리고 동네 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: I took the yellow dog for a walk around the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 누렁이 덕분에 밤에도 집이 무섭지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the yellow dog, the house isn't scary even at night.

explain: 누런 털을 가진 개를 친근하게 부르는 말이에요. '바둑이'처럼 털 색깔로 붙인 흔한 개 이름이기도 해요. 부를 때는 '누렁아'라고 해요.

phrases.en: When I call "Nureong-a," he comes wagging his tail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개를 부를 때는 '누렁이'의 '이'를 '아'로 바꿔서 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: To call the dog, change the '이' of '누렁이' to '아'.

phrases.en: My grandmother keeps a yellow dog at her house in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개를 기른다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation meaning to raise a dog.

phrases.en: The yellow dog barked loudly at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이/가'를 붙여서 개가 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '이/가' it describes what the dog does.

explain_en: It is an affectionate name for a dog with a yellow coat. Like '바둑이', it is also a typical dog name based on coat appearance. When calling it, you say '누렁아'.

examples.en: As a child, I caught freshwater snails in the stream.
Freshwater snails live only in clean water.
There are so many snails along the stream.
The kids looked at the snails and the tadpoles.
Soup made with freshwater snails tastes refreshing.

examples.ko: 다슬기 수제비를 먹어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever tried freshwater snail sujebi?

explain: 강이나 개울에 사는 작은 고둥으로, 국이나 수제비 재료로 먹어요. 지역에 따라 '올갱이'라고 부르는 곳도 있어요.

phrases.en: In summer I caught freshwater snails in the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개울에서 직접 잡는 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about catching them yourself in a stream.

phrases.en: I had freshwater snail soup to cure my hangover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 음식 이름으로 쓰고, 해장국으로 유명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a dish, well known as a hangover soup.

phrases.en: In Chungcheong they call freshwater snails 'olgaengi.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역에 따라 다슬기를 부르는 다른 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A regional name for the freshwater snail.

explain_en: It is a small freshwater snail living in rivers and streams, eaten in soup or sujebi. In some regions people call it '올갱이'.

en: to be clear and sunny; to be fine (weather)

examples.en: The sky is really clear today.

examples.ko: 날씨가 쾌청해서 소풍 가기 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: The weather is clear, so it's perfect for a picnic.
The rain has stopped, so the sky is clear.
They say it will be clear all over the country tomorrow.

examples.ko: 쾌청한 가을 하늘 아래에서 운동회를 했어요.
examples.en: We had a sports day under the clear autumn sky.
If the weather is clear this weekend, do you want to go to the Han River?

explain: '맑다'보다 구름이 거의 없이 상쾌하게 갠 날씨를 말해요. 날씨 예보나 글에서 자주 보이고, 보통 날씨나 하늘에만 써요. '맑다'는 물이나 눈, 목소리에도 쓰지만 '쾌청하다'는 그렇게 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Walking in the clear weather puts me in a good mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이에요. 날씨 이야기에 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, best suited to talking about weather.

phrases.en: Yesterday the sky was clear all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이에요. 이미 지나간 날씨를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, describing weather that has already passed.

phrases.example: 쾌청한 가을 하늘 아래에서 운동회를 했어요.
phrases.en: We held the sports day under a clear autumn sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절과 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 특히 가을 하늘과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A frequent pairing with seasons, especially the autumn sky.

explain_en: It describes weather that is clear and refreshing with almost no clouds, which is stronger than '맑다'. It often appears in weather forecasts and writing, and it is used only for weather or the sky. '맑다' also works for water, eyes or voices, but '쾌청하다' does not.

t90.ax: The sky is really clear today.

examples.en: My friends snickered behind me and looked at me.
I giggled to myself while reading a comic book.
If you snicker during class, the teacher will scold you.
The two are whispering and giggling.
What's so funny that you're snickering like that?
The sound of giggling could be heard all the way to the hallway.

explain: 혼자 재미있어하거나 남을 놀리듯이 목구멍에서 새어 나오는 소리로 웃는 모습이에요. 때로는 놀리거나 비웃는 느낌도 있어요. 밝고 시원하게 크게 웃는 '깔깔거리다'와 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: The friends in the back keep snickering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낄낄거리다'와 거의 같고 조금 더 줄여서 말하는 입말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 낄낄거리다, a shorter spoken form.

phrases.en: My younger sibling giggles while watching a video.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낄낄'을 부사처럼 앞에 붙여 웃는 소리를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 낄낄 as an adverb to show the sound of laughing.

phrases.en: Please don't snicker during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 하라고 부탁하거나 주의를 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to stop snickering.

explain_en: Near-synonym of 낄낄대다; the -거리다 form of a stifled, snickering laugh that can be mocking (뒤에서 낄낄거리다). It describes laughing in a sniggering way, with sounds leaking out from the throat, either amused to yourself or at someone's expense. Sometimes it suggests teasing or mocking. It feels different from '깔깔거리다', which is a bright, hearty laugh.

t90.ax: The two are whispering and giggling.

en: to be sulky; to be glum

examples.ko: 동생이 하루 종일 뚱해서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My younger brother has been sulky all day and isn't talking.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 뚱한 얼굴로 앉아 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you sitting there with such a sulky face?
He answered sullenly, as if he were upset.
The child who got scolded is sulking.

examples.ko: 표정이 뚱하고 말이 없어서 걱정이 됐어요.
examples.en: He looked sulky and silent, so I was worried.
My friend was late, so I was in a sulky mood.

explain: '뚱뚱하다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요. 못마땅하거나 기분이 안 좋아서 말없이 퉁명스러운 표정이나 태도를 보일 때 써요. '뚱한 표정', '뚱하게 앉아 있다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 아침부터 뚱한 표정으로 아무 말도 안 해요.
phrases.en: He's had a sulky look since morning and says nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뚱한 + 명사'로 기분이 안 좋아 보이는 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '뚱한 + noun' describes a face that looks sulky.

phrases.en: The child answered sullenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뚱하게'는 말하는 방식을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: 뚱하게 describes the way someone speaks.

phrases.example: 오늘 기분이 안 좋아요? 좀 뚱해 보여요.
phrases.en: Are you in a bad mood today? You look a bit sulky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습을 보고 말할 때 '뚱해 보이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 뚱해 보이다 when judging by how someone looks.

explain_en: It is completely different from '뚱뚱하다' (fat). It describes a sulky, silent look or attitude when someone is displeased or in a bad mood. Common patterns are '뚱한 표정' and '뚱하게 앉아 있다'.

en: to be calm; to be unmoved

examples.en: Even after hearing the news of the breakup, he seemed unfazed.
The indifferent way you answered hurt me a little.
I cried at first, but now I feel calm about it.
He had a deadpan look even after receiving a present.

examples.ko: 무덤덤하다고 해서 아무 감정이 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because someone seems unmoved doesn't mean they have no feelings.

examples.ko: 아버지는 무덤덤해 보여도 속으로는 걱정이 많으세요.
examples.en: My father looks unbothered, but inside he worries a lot.

explain: 겉으로 감정을 잘 드러내지 않거나 별로 마음이 흔들리지 않는 모습에 쓰는 일상적인 말이에요. 속으로는 감정이 있을 수도 있어서 '무감동하다'보다 부드러워요. 말투나 태도가 퉁명스러운 '무뚝뚝하다'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: He was sitting there with an unmoved look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 얼굴에 잘 드러나지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when emotion doesn't show on the face.

phrases.en: She talked about the hard time in a flat, calm way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정을 크게 싣지 않고 말하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking without putting much emotion into it.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak in a flat, calm tone

phrases.en: As time passed, I've become unaffected by it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에는 흔들렸던 마음이 점점 조용해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feelings that once stirred have quieted down.

explain_en: It is an everyday word for someone who doesn't show feelings outwardly or isn't much shaken. They may still have feelings inside, so it is softer than '무감동하다'. It differs from '무뚝뚝하다', which describes a curt, blunt manner of speaking or acting.

t90.ax: I cried at first, but now I feel calm about it.

examples.ko: 사장님이 거짓말을 알고 발칵 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The boss found out about the lie and suddenly flew into a rage.

examples.ko: 시험지가 바뀌었다는 소식에 학교가 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: The school was thrown into an uproar at the news that the exam papers had been mixed up.

examples.ko: 형이 발칵 소리를 질러서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My older brother suddenly yelled, and it startled me.

examples.ko: 친구가 별것 아닌 일로 발칵 짜증을 냈어요.
examples.en: My friend suddenly got irritated over something trivial.
The door suddenly flew open and everyone was startled.

examples.ko: 회사 비밀이 새어 나가자 사무실이 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: When the company secret leaked out, the office was in an uproar.

explain: 갑자기 화를 내거나 소란이 일어날 때 써요. '발칵 화내다', '발칵 뒤집히다'처럼 짝으로 많이 나와요. 비슷한 '왈칵'은 눈물이나 감정이 갑자기 쏟아질 때 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 사라졌다는 소식에 온 동네가 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
phrases.en: At the news that the child had disappeared, the whole neighborhood was in an uproar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 뒤집히는 게 아니라, 어떤 일 때문에 사람들이 놀라고 크게 술렁이는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean something is flipped over; it means people are shocked and a place is thrown into a big stir over some event.

explain_en: It is used when anger or a commotion breaks out suddenly. It often appears in pairs like '발칵 화내다' and '발칵 뒤집히다'. The similar '왈칵' is used when tears or emotions suddenly burst out.

t90.ax: My older brother suddenly yelled, and it startled me.

examples.en: My younger sibling sulked because they couldn't get the toy.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 말에 삐쳐서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My friend is sulking over what I said and won't talk to me.

examples.ko: 별것도 아닌 일로 자꾸 삐치지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't keep sulking over trivial things.

examples.ko: 남자친구가 삐친 것 같은데 어떻게 풀어 줘야 할까요?
examples.en: My boyfriend seems sulky. How should I make it up to him?

examples.ko: 아이가 삐치면 한참 동안 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: When my child sulks, he doesn't talk for quite a while.
He's really sulking, so apologize first.

explain: 크게 화내는 것보다 서운해서 말을 안 하거나 토라지는 가벼운 감정이에요. 친구, 연인, 가족처럼 가까운 사이에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '삐지다'라고도 자주 해요. 비슷한 '토라지다'와 가까운 말이에요.

phrases.example: 동생이 또 삐져서 말을 안 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is sulking again and won't talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삐치다'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 삐치다, used more often in speech.

phrases.en: The child sulked and went into the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서운해서 마음이 틀어지는 느낌이고, '삐치다'와 가까운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A feeling of turning away out of hurt, close in meaning to 삐치다.

phrases.en: It was just a joke, so please don't sulk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 사이에서 달랠 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to soothe someone close to you.

explain_en: It is a mild feeling of being hurt and going quiet, not full-blown anger. It is used among close people like friends, partners and family, and in speech people often say '삐지다' too. '토라지다' is a close synonym.
